kicker: Latent Sparse Attention, from the paper

scenes.headline: How LSA finds the keys without scoring them all
scenes.sub: Cluster the keys by meaning, then search the clusters.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ladle! Sparse attention reads only a few thousand keys per query. Something still has to choose them. Here is how Latent Sparse Attention makes that choice cheap.

scenes.text: Group keys into buckets of about 8 by meaning, and let each query score one centroid per bucket instead of every key.
scenes.say: Group the keys into small buckets by meaning. Then each query scores one centroid per bucket, instead of every single key.

steps.say: Each key is projected to a small index space and normalised.
Every four neighbouring keys are summed into one pool key.
When a block of five hundred and twelve keys is full, Ward's method merges the closest pools, round after round.
Each bucket keeps a centroid and the positions of its keys. It never changes again.

scenes.title: Then search them per query
scenes.say: A query now does four small things.

items.text: Sum the heads into one query
items.say: Sum the query heads into one index query.
Score the bucket centroids, not the keys.
Expand them into their keys, add the sink and the window, and attend.

steps.say: At ten million tokens, the indexer is ninety-eight percent of a sparse layer's prefill time.

scenes.title: One layer at 10M tokens, prefill
scenes.note: reported, one H200; whole Qwen model 9.21x to first token
scenes.say: The paper reports one layer twenty-two times faster than GLM's own sparse attention, and seventy-two times faster than full attention. The whole model gains about nine times.

left.title: Pools of 4
items: beats blocks of 8 at equal work
left.say: In my port, the shipped design beats positional blocks at the same index cost, and loses to blocks of four.

right.title: No pooling
right.say: Turn the pooling off, and scattered related keys are found again, at a higher clustering cost.

scenes.text: Past a million tokens, the cost of sparse attention is finding the keys, and clusters make finding them cheap.
scenes.say: Past a million tokens, the cost of sparse attention is finding the keys. Clusters make finding them cheap.

recap: The indexer dominates at long context
Ward buckets replace the key scan
It pays past one million tokens
scenes.say: The indexer dominates long context. Buckets replace the scan. And it pays past a million tokens.
